as_written_in_papers.quote: a novel heterozygote mutation P507S (c.1519C>T) in the fourth exon of the NOD2 gene was revealed
Analysis of the protein variant revealed that the mutation was p.Pro507Ser.

cases.statement: One person: a boy (identity BLAU-ID0085), heterozygous, with infantile rash, symmetrical polyarthritis with tenosynovial cysts of the hand dorsum, and granulomatous anterior uveitis at 5 years.

people.label: patient
people.other_allele: not applicable (autosomal dominant); the paper reports no second NOD2 variant
people.key_phenotypes: maculopapular erythematous rash from 5 months; swelling of hand dorsum with tenosynovial cysts; symmetrical arthritis of knees, wrists and ankles; granulomatous anterior uveitis (right eye) at 5 years

quotes.quote: A 5-year-old male was initially admitted to our clinic at 5 months of age with a maculopapular erythematous rash over his entire body (Figures 1 and 2).
Ultrasonography of the swelling, performed at another facility, revealed tenosynovial cysts.
Four months after the first swelling appeared, the patient presented at our hospital with symmetrical arthritis of both knees.
Four months after treatment commenced, we detected symmetrical arthritis of both wrists and ankles.

During follow-up at 5 years of age, the ophthalmological examination revealed granulomatous anterior uveitis in the patient's right eye, as indicated by large precipitates in the anterior chamber and nodules in the iris.

phenotype_specificity.statement: The authors describe the rash, symmetrical arthritis and granulomatous uveitis as the classic Blau triad and revised an initial JIA diagnosis to Blau syndrome. RF and ANA were negative. No skin biopsy of this patient is described (the sentence on noncaseating granulomas cites a reference). Only NOD2 was tested; no other genes or panels are reported.

quotes.quote: The classic triad of the disease includes recurrent uveitis, granulomatous dermatitis, and symmetrical arthritis; however, all symptoms may not appear concurrently [2].
Thus, the presence of skin lesions, granulomatous ophthalmologic inflammation, and the NOD2 gene mutation ruled out the diagnosis of JIA.
rheumatoid factor 6 IU/mL (normal level, <16), and antinuclear antibody negative
Genetic studies were run to investigate the NOD2 gene mutation.

segregation.statement: No relatives were genotyped. The family history was negative and the parents were described as healthy.

quotes.quote: The patient's family history revealed no inherited familial disease.
Although Blau syndrome is an AD inherited disease, the parents of the patient were healthy.

de_novo.statement: Assumed by the authors, not shown: the parents are described as healthy, but no parental genotyping and no parentage confirmation are reported.

quotes.quote: Although Blau syndrome is an AD inherited disease, the parents of the patient were healthy.
Blau syndrome resulting fromde novo mutations may present sporadically [7], and we believe ade novo mutation caused the Blau syndrome in our case.

functional.statement: No assay of this variant is reported. The authors state they found no data that it causes NF-kappa B hyperactivation.

quotes.quote: We found no data to indicate that this mutation caused NF-kappa B hyperactivation.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense (predicted p.Pro480Ser on NP_001357395.1). The paper makes no statement on the disease mechanism.

computational_predictions.statement: The authors report an in-silico assessment with SIFT, MutationTaster and PolyPhen but give no individual scores or calls.

quotes.quote: In silico assessment (SIFT, Mutation Taster, and Polyphen) of the mutation indicated a strong association with Blau syndrome.

population_data_in_papers.statement: No control or population frequency data are given; the authors state only that the variant has not been reported previously.

quotes.quote: This heterozygous NOD2 gene mutation has not been reported previously.

authors_classification.statement: The authors call it a novel (de novo) mutation causing Blau syndrome; no ACMG criteria are given.

quotes.quote: Here, we describe a novel sporadic gene mutation causing Blau syndrome that has not been reported previously.
Here, we described ade novo mutation causing Blau syndrome that has not been reported previously.

concerns: Legacy numbering: the paper writes c.1519C>T / p.Pro507Ser (no transcript stated); the batch places it as NM_001370466.1:c.1438C>T, predicted p.(Pro480Ser). The 81-nt and 27-residue offsets match the older NM_022162 numbering (protein_check: differs, stated P507S, predicted P480S). The panel should confirm the placement.
The de novo status is the authors' belief only; no parental testing or parentage confirmation is reported.

The genetic sentence is oddly worded ('The results showed only a P507S mutation; however, a novel heterozygote mutation P507S ... was revealed'); it is unclear which exons were sequenced and whether other NOD2 variants were sought.
The in-silico statement gives no scores, and 'strong association with Blau syndrome' is not a standard predictor output.

No skin biopsy of this patient is described; the sentence 'The histologic examination of the skin lesions revealed noncaseating granulomatous disease [5]' cites a reference and reads as literature background, so granulomas are not shown for this person.
Short case report; single person; no second report of this patient in the batch papers.
notes_for_panel: Single sporadic case in a short report. Phenotype is the classic triad, but the evidence is thin: no parental genotyping, no functional assay, in-silico statement without scores, and legacy cDNA/protein numbering (c.1519C>T / P507S) that the batch translated to MANE c.1438C>T / P480S.
